all_comments.text:
This is a useful tips video, but I think it mixes three different things together: real iPhone 17 Pro hardware features, iOS 26 features, and sponsored accessory talk. That does not make the video useless, but it is worth separating them, because not everything here is actually specific to the 17 Pro or 17 Pro Max.

The camera stuff is probably the most relevant part. The new 18 MP Center Stage front camera is actually one of the more practical upgrades, because being able to switch between portrait and landscape framing without physically rotating the phone is useful if you record yourself, do video calls, or make quick clips. Dual Capture is also useful, especially for vlog-style recording, because front and rear camera recording at the same time is something people will actually use.

But the rear camera part needs a bit more context. Yes, all three rear cameras are 48 MP now, and yes, 4x and 8x are useful. But 8x is not the same thing as having a real 200 mm lens. On the 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max, 1x is around 24 mm, 2x is around 48 mm, 4x is around 100 mm, and 8x is around 200 mm full-frame equivalent. That sounds more meaningful than just saying “8x zoom.” But the 8x mode is still 12 MP “optical-quality,” meaning it is using crop/processing from the telephoto sensor, not a separate true 200 mm optical lens.

That is why I wish phone videos would stop talking only in x-zoom. I use a Nikon D7500, and my 70-200 mm on that crop sensor is roughly 105-300 mm full-frame equivalent. So even that lens is already tighter at the long end than the iPhone’s 8x. That does not mean the iPhone camera is bad. It is impressive for a phone. But “40x zoom” is digital zoom, and at that point people need realistic expectations. It is not magic glass. It is a phone using a small sensor, processing, and a lot of software.

The battery tips are more useful than they sound, but Adaptive Power should also be explained properly. It can help stretch battery life, but it does that by making small performance adjustments, lowering brightness, and limiting background activity. So if someone is filming, gaming, navigating, or using the phone hard, they should understand what it does instead of just turning it on blindly. Battery-saving features are always a trade-off somewhere.

Call Screening is probably one of the best practical features here. Unknown callers are a pain, and having the phone ask for the caller’s name and reason before bothering you is genuinely useful. But again, that is more of an iOS 26 feature than an iPhone 17 Pro Max feature. Same with lock screen customization, app icon styles, iMessage backgrounds, animated album art, battery percentage, Visual Intelligence from screenshots, and a lot of the “hidden” stuff. Good tips, but not all of them require buying a 17 Pro.

The spatial photo / spatial wallpaper thing is cool, but I see it more as a fun visual feature than a reason to buy the phone. It is one of those things people will play with a lot for the first week, then only use when it actually fits a good photo. Same with tinted icons and clear icons. Nice to have, but not something I would call a Pro feature.

The ringtone part is interesting, because Apple has made custom ringtones easier over time, but I would still be careful how it is presented. Traditionally, Apple’s official method for custom ringtones has involved GarageBand, and ringtones have the 30-second limit. If Files-to-ringtone is now showing directly for short MP3 files, that is a good change, but it is also one of those things that can vary depending on file type, DRM, and where the audio came from.

The case and screen protector section is where I get more skeptical, mostly because it turns into sponsored accessory talk. I agree that using a case and screen protector makes sense on a phone this expensive. But “same manufacturer as Apple’s cover glass” does not automatically mean the screen protector performs like Apple’s actual glass. Manufacturing source is not the same thing as final design, coating, lamination, hardness, drop protection, or quality control. A good third-party case can absolutely be better value than Apple’s cases, but I would judge it by fit, raised edges, MagSafe strength, camera bump protection, button feel, and how it works with Camera Control.

The Camera Control customization tip is one of the better ones. Turning off the options you do not use and leaving only zoom or exposure makes sense, because otherwise it can feel like you are fighting the button instead of using it. Personally, I would rather have fewer controls that I actually use than five modes I accidentally scroll through.

So overall, good video for new users, but I would not frame all of this as “iPhone 17 Pro tricks.” A lot of it is iOS 26, some of it is camera hardware, and some of it is sponsored accessories. The useful stuff is Call Screening, Camera Control customization, Dual Capture, 48 MP resolution control, Adaptive Power, and knowing what 4x/8x actually means. The less useful stuff is the flashy customization unless someone really cares about making the phone look different.

For me, the important thing is still whether the phone works as a tool. I use both iPhone and Android daily, and I also use a real camera, so I do not really care about brand worship. I care about what works. The 17 Pro/Pro Max cameras and video features are serious for a phone, but people should still understand the limits instead of just hearing “48 MP,” “8x,” and “40x zoom” and thinking it replaces real camera gear.

and in the corner, you'll see this new icon. Tap it, then wait a few seconds and tilt your iPhone, because vah-bam!

You can do this with any picture you've taken on the iPhone 17 Pro and even pictures you've downloaded.

Then tap on the P to quickly get to the phone application. Scroll down again to this new section called Screen Unknown Callers, and change it to Ask Reason for Calling.
Because now, when you get a call from someone not saved as a contact, not only will your iPhone automatically answer for you,
but it'll also say this. Hi, if you record your name and reason for calling, I'll see if this person is available.
Then once it gets all that info, it'll ring and show you what the other person said,
so you can choose whether to answer or not. I mean, that is so damn nifty.
As for my next Pro trick, this one is hidden inside battery settings, then under power mode, and it's called adaptive power.
Make sure you turn this on, because when you do, your iPhone will stretch out its power as much as possible
by making different adjustments to basically get the best battery life possible.
Neat! But that's not even the best trick yet. Because now, open up your camera, because there's a lot of new things I've got to show you.
Okay, so now, every back camera on the 17 Pro and Pro Max is 48 megapixels.

which literally switches between portrait and landscape mode.

and your arm is never in the way, compared to shooting in landscape.

But here's a really fun new trick you can do with both the front and the back cameras.

which is the highest resolution. And so when you take a 0.5, 1x, or 4x picture,
